title: Accepting a job offer

items.title: The pay is broken down
items.look_for: Fixed pay, variable pay and what is guaranteed each month
items.why_it_matters: A headline figure can include amounts you may never receive
items.question_to_ask: How much of this reaches my bank account each month?

items.title: Conditions on the variable part are stated
items.look_for: What the bonus depends on and when it is paid
items.why_it_matters: A bonus with undefined conditions is not a promise
items.question_to_ask: What exactly has to happen for the variable pay to be paid?

items.title: The joining date and place are fixed
items.look_for: A start date and a work location or a remote arrangement
items.why_it_matters: An unstated location can become a transfer you did not plan for
items.question_to_ask: Where will I be based, and can that change?

items.title: The probation terms are stated
items.look_for: Length of probation and the notice period during it
items.why_it_matters: Notice during probation is often much shorter
items.question_to_ask: How long is probation and what notice applies during it?

items.title: The notice period is stated for both sides
items.look_for: How much notice you must give and how much you would receive
items.why_it_matters: A long notice period can block your next job
items.question_to_ask: Is the notice period the same for both sides, and can it be bought out?

items.title: Any service bond and its cost are clear
items.look_for: A minimum period you must stay and the amount payable if you leave
items.why_it_matters: A bond can make leaving expensive for years
items.question_to_ask: What exactly would I owe if I left after one year?

items.title: Any joining bonus clawback is stated
items.look_for: A requirement to repay a joining bonus or relocation cost
items.why_it_matters: A clawback can arrive as an unexpected bill after you resign
items.question_to_ask: Would I have to repay the joining bonus, and on what timetable?

items.title: Any restriction after leaving is narrow
items.look_for: Limits on where you may work next, for how long and in what area
items.why_it_matters: A broad restriction can limit your next role
items.question_to_ask: Which companies or roles would this stop me from taking?

items.title: Working hours and leave are stated
items.look_for: Expected hours, weekly off and annual leave
items.why_it_matters: Leave and hours are what you actually live with day to day
items.question_to_ask: What are the working hours and how much leave do I get?

items.title: Exit documents are promised
items.look_for: A commitment to issue a relieving letter and experience letter
items.why_it_matters: The next employer usually asks for these
items.question_to_ask: When would I receive my relieving and experience letters?

items.title: Final settlement has a deadline
items.look_for: A number of days within which dues are settled after leaving
items.why_it_matters: Without a date, a pending settlement can drag on
items.question_to_ask: Within how many days of my last day will dues be settled?

items.title: What the company owns is defined
items.look_for: Wording about work you create, and whether it extends outside work hours
items.why_it_matters: Very broad wording can cover personal projects
items.question_to_ask: Does this cover work I do on my own time?

items.title: The grounds for termination are listed
items.look_for: Reasons the company may end employment and whether notice applies
items.why_it_matters: It tells you what protection you actually have
items.question_to_ask: On what grounds can employment be ended, and with what notice?

suggested_questions: Is there a service bond, and what would it cost me to leave early?
What happens to my joining bonus if I resign within a year?
What restrictions apply after I leave?
When would I receive my relieving letter?

scenarios.title: I am let go during probation
I join a competitor after leaving
The offer is withdrawn before I join

facts_to_have_ready: The date you received the offer and the date you are expected to join
Your current notice period, if you are employed
Any amount already paid to you, such as a joining bonus
Emails or messages about the terms you were promised
documents_to_bring: The offer letter and any annexures
The appointment letter, if it is different
Any bond or undertaking you were asked to sign
Payslips, if the dispute is about pay
